title: Galois Epp preparation with reduced special fibre
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $d\geq2$ and mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Normal means integrally closed in its fraction field. There exist a complete Noetherian normal local domain $(C,\mathfrak n)$, an injective module-finite local map $A\to C$, a complete discrete valuation ring $W$ of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with perfect residue field $k_0$, an injective local map $W\to C$, and a finite group $G$ acting compatibly on $W$ and $C$ by local automorphisms and fixing $A$ pointwise [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The fraction-field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(C)/\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ is finite Galois with $G$ identified with its full group of automorphisms; finite Galois means finite-dimensional, normal and separable algebraic [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. For a uniformizer $\pi$ of $W$, $C/\pi C$ is reduced and equidimensional of dimension $d-1$, $\dim C=d$, and $C/\mathfrak n$ is finite over $A/\mathfrak m$ and contains $k_0$. Reduced means no nonzero nilpotents; equidimensional means all quotients by minimal prime ideals have the indicated dimension; perfect means bijective Frobenius. No formal power-series presentation is asserted.

source.place: Exposé IV 4.3.3–4.3.5, p.60: finite constant extension made Galois before normalized base change, together with the reduced-fibre argument 4.2.3–4.2.4 and the generic Galois observation in 4.3.7, p.61. Equivalently one can take a component and its decomposition group.

proof.text: Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and $k_*=\bigcap_{n\ge0}k^{p^n}$. This intersection is a field, and is perfect: the unique $p$th root of an element in all $k^{p^n}$ again lies in all $k^{p^n}$. Choose a Cohen ring $W_0$ with residue field $k_*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist], and use [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] for completeness, the DVR property, and uniformizer $p$. Construct compatible maps $g_n:W_0/p^n\to A/\mathfrak m^n$ starting with the given inclusion $k_*\to k$. Given $g_n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth] with exponent $n+1$, target $A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and square-zero ideal $\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ to lift the composite from $W_0/p^{n+1}$. Here $p^{n+1}=0$ in the target since $p\in\mathfrak m$. Completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] gives a ring map $W_0\to A$ from these compatible maps. It is local because its residue map is injective. It is injective: every nonzero element of $W_0$ is $up^a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], with $u$ a unit, and $p^a\ne0$ in the characteristic-zero domain $A$.

source.place: IV 4.2.3, coefficient map from 4.1.8; lifting construction also Stacks Tags 0328, 0329

proof.text: Let $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ be the minimal primes over $pA$; they are finite by [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal]. Each $P_i$ is a minimal support prime of the cyclic module $A/pA$, hence associated by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated], and has height one by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-principal-quotient-associated-height]. The localization $T_i=A_{P_i}$ is Noetherian and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], of dimension one, so is a DVR by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. The map $W_0\to T_i$ is injective and local since its uniformizer $p$ belongs to $P_i$. The ring $A$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], and each $T_i$ is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent].

source.place: IV 4.2.3, finitely many generic points of the special fibre

proof.text: The residue field of $T_i$ is $\operatorname{Frac}(A/P_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], $R_i=A/P_i$ is a complete Noetherian local domain of characteristic $p$ with residue field $k$. The map $k_*=W_0/pW_0\to R_i$ is injective because it is a unital map from a field to a nonzero ring. Its composite with $R_i\to k$ is the original inclusion. Since $k_{\mathrm{perf}}=k_*$, [lem-per-epp-perfect-core-complete-local] proves that every element of the maximal perfect subfield of $\operatorname{Frac}(A/P_i)$ is algebraic over $k_*$. Apply [lem-per-epp-finite-family-traits] to all the $T_i$ at once, obtaining a finite extension $W_0\hookrightarrow W_1$ of complete DVRs, with perfect residue field. Put $K_*=\operatorname{Frac}(W_0)$ and $K_1=\operatorname{Frac}(W_1)$. The extension $W_1$ is good for every $T_i$, in the explicit sense of [lem-per-epp-single-trait-base-change]: every normalized field factor of the base change has reduced special fibre.

source.place: IV 4.2.3, use of 3.2.3(i),(iv) and simultaneous Epp theorem

proof.text: The extension $K_1/K_*$ is finite. Indeed, localizing a finite $W_0$-module generating set for $W_1$ gives a finite-dimensional domain over $K_*$. Multiplication by any nonzero element is an injective endomorphism of this vector space, hence surjective; this localization is a field and therefore equals $K_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension], embed $K_1$ in an extension $K$ finite and normal over $K_*$. It is separable: in characteristic zero an irreducible polynomial of positive degree has nonzero derivative of smaller degree, so it is relatively prime to its derivative. Thus $K/K_*$ is finite Galois.

source.place: IV 4.3.5, making the finite constant extension generically Galois; Stacks Tag 09DT (fields-lemma-normal-closure).

proof.text: Let $W$ be the integral closure of $W_0$ in $K$. By [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization], $W$ is a finite complete DVR over $W_0$, with fraction field $K$, and $W_0\to W$ is local. Moreover $W_1\subseteq W$: the elements of $W_1$ satisfy monic equations over $W_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. The map $W_1\to W$ is local. If $\pi_1$ is a uniformizer of $W_1$, write $p=u\pi_1^a$ with $a>0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]; since $p$ lies in the maximal ideal of $W$ and $u$ is a unit, so does $\pi_1$, whereas every element outside $(\pi_1)$ remains a unit. The residue field $k_0=W/\mathfrak m_W$ is finite over $k_*$: a finite $W_0$-module generating set descends to a spanning set. It is perfect by [lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect]. For each $i$, apply clause (3) of [lem-per-epp-single-trait-base-change] to $W_1\to W$; all normalized field factors over $W$ still have reduced special fibre. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $W$.

source.place: IV 4.3.5 together with IV 4.2.3, stability of Epp preparation under finite constant extension; Stacks Tags 09EM, 09F8 (remark-construction, lemma-special-case).

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. The algebra $F\otimes_{K_*}K$ is nonzero and finite dimensional over $F$: tensor a $K_*$-basis of $K$. Choose a maximal ideal and let $L$ be its quotient field. Then $L/F$ is finite and the unital map $K\to L$ is injective. Let $C\subset L$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. It is a normal domain with fraction field $L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]. It is finite over $A$: [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] and [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring, def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] give precisely this for the finite extension $L/F$. The map $A\to C$ is injective, and $W\subset C$, because $W$ is finite over $W_0$ and hence integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; its monic equations over $W_0$ are also monic equations over $A$.

source.place: IV 4.2.3 and first sentence of 4.2.5, choosing a component of the normalized base change

proof.text: The images of $F$ and $K$ generate $L$ as a field: the surjection $F\otimes_{K_*}K\to L$ expresses every element of $L$ as a finite sum of products from these two images. Apply [lem-per-galois-compositum-restriction] to these subfields of $L$. The extension $L/F$ is Galois, and each $F$-automorphism of $L$ preserves $K$. It is already finite by the preceding step. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] shows that $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$ is finite. This is the full group required in the statement, and restriction gives its action on $K$. We do not identify $G$ with all of $\operatorname{Aut}_{K_*}(K)$; it may be a proper subgroup.

source.place: IV 4.3.7, generic Galois group a subgroup of the constant-extension group; compositum calculation in Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean:557,608,623.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product], the finite $A$-domain $C$ is Noetherian complete local, with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ over $\mathfrak m$. Thus $A\hookrightarrow C$ is local. The field $k'=C/\mathfrak n$ is finite over $k$: the images of any finite $A$-module generating set of $C$ span $k'$ over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal], $\dim C=d$. Also $W\hookrightarrow C$ is local: in $W$ the nonzero element $p$ is $u\pi^e$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]; its residue is zero, so $e>0$. Since $p\in\mathfrak n$ and $u$ stays a unit, $\pi\in\mathfrak n$. Every element outside $\pi W$ is a unit, giving the asserted inverse image of $\mathfrak n$. Reduction supplies the specified inclusion $k_0\hookrightarrow k'$.

source.place: IV 4.2.5, first sentence and residue fields

proof.text: For $g\in G$, applying $g$ to a monic equation over $A$ leaves its coefficients fixed, so $g(C)\subseteq C$; applying $g^{-1}$ gives equality. Likewise, restriction to $K$ fixes $K_*$, hence $W_0$, so monic equations over $W_0$ show $g(W)=W$. The restrictions are ring automorphisms and form compatible actions because they are restrictions of the same action on $L$. A ring automorphism preserves the unique maximal ideal of a local ring, so these automorphisms of $C$ and $W$ are local. The action fixes $A$ pointwise by the definition of $G$. Under $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=L$, it is exactly the full Galois action. The map $W\to C$ is the inclusion already constructed, so it is equivariant.

source.place: IV 4.3.5–4.3.7, action on the normalization and the coefficient DVR; applying automorphisms to the defining monic equations.

proof.text: Let $Q$ be a height-one prime of $C$ containing $\pi$ and put $P=Q\cap A$. It contains $p$ because $p=u\pi^e$. Going down for the normal domain $A$ in its integral domain extension $C$ [lem-weil-pbc-going-down-normal-integral] shows that $P$ cannot have a strict chain of length two below it: such a chain would lift to one below $Q$. Since $p\ne0$, $P$ has height one. Hence $P$ is minimal over $pA$ (a strictly smaller prime containing $p$ would give a chain of length two), and equals some $P_i$.

source.place: IV 4.2.3, parenthesis about generic points above generic points; Stacks Tag 00H8

proof.text: Fix this $P_i$ and localize $C$ at $A\setminus P_i$, obtaining $C_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $C_i$ is the integral closure of $T_i=A_{P_i}$ in $L$ (localizing the field $L$ changes nothing). Let $D_i$ be the image of $T_i\otimes_{W_0}W$ in $L$. It is integral over $T_i$ by the finite-algebra criterion [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]: a finite $W_0$-module generating set of $W$ gives one for this image over $T_i$. If $x\in L$ is integral over $D_i$, the extension $D_i\subset D_i[x]$ is integral: the powers below the degree of a monic equation span $D_i[x]$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] applies. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] for $T_i\subset D_i\subset D_i[x]$ makes $x$ integral over $T_i$. Conversely a monic equation over $T_i$ is one over $D_i$. Thus $C_i$ is exactly the integral closure of $D_i$ in $L$. Since $\operatorname{Frac}(T_i)=F$, the field $L$ is a field factor of $F\otimes_{K_*}K$. The goodness of $W$ for $T_i$ proved in step 5, namely clause (3) of [lem-per-epp-single-trait-base-change], therefore says that $C_i/\pi C_i$ is reduced.

source.place: IV 4.2.3, normalized base change localized at a generic point

proof.text: The ring $C_Q/\pi C_Q$ is reduced. Indeed, it is a localization of the reduced ring $C_i/\pi C_i$: the maps identify fractions $c/s$ and impose the same relation $\pi=0$. To check reducedness directly, if $(x/s)^n=0$, some inverted $t$ has $tx^n=0$, so $(tx)^n=t^{n-1}(tx^n)=0$; reducedness gives $tx=0$, hence $x/s=0$. This proves the generic reducedness assertion for every height-one $Q$ containing $\pi$.

source.place: IV 4.2.3, passage to the local special fibre

proof.text: Set $M=C/\pi C$. Every associated prime $Q$ of this cyclic $C$-module has height one by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-principal-quotient-associated-height], because $C$ is a Noetherian normal domain and $\pi\ne0$. Such a prime contains $\pi$. If $z\in M$ is nilpotent, its image in $M_Q=C_Q/\pi C_Q$ is zero by the preceding step; the identification is [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient]. Injectivity into the product of these module localizations [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] forces $z=0$. Thus $C/\pi C$ is reduced. This is the argument of IV 4.2.4, expressed through the already available associated-prime form of Stacks 031T and 0311.

The complete Noetherian local domain $C$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], hence catenary by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Every prime $Q$ minimal over $\pi C$ is a minimal support prime of $C/\pi C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated] and [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-principal-quotient-associated-height] give $\operatorname{ht}(Q)=1$. In the catenary local domain $C$ of dimension $d$, all saturated chains from $(0)$ to $\mathfrak n$ have length $d$. A saturated chain from $Q$ to $\mathfrak n$, preceded by $(0)\subsetneq Q$, is such a chain, so has length $d-1$ above $Q$. Chains in $C/Q$ are exactly chains above $Q$; therefore $\dim(C/Q)=d-1$ for every minimal $Q$ of $C/\pi C$. This proves equidimensionality of the required dimension. The construction of $C,W,\pi$ and the residue inclusions in the preceding steps supplies every remaining clause.

source.place: IV 4.2.5, assertion that the reduced special fibre is equidimensional of dimension d-1
